items.headline: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut
items.blurb: Anthropic is the first purely AI company to be publicly listed, creating a test for the entire industry.
items.text: Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the public stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion. The artificial intelligence (AI) company's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange was a crucial test for the industry, given the huge amount of money being poured into advancing the technology. Anthropic's shares flew past its allocation price of $83 per share , showing there is plenty of excitement around AI. Yet the company, which is behind AI chatbot Claude, will remain under intense scrutiny in the months ahead to answer the key question surrounding AI: is it all worth it? In just a few hours of trading, Anthropic's stock seemed to show that investors remain uncertain of where exactly AI is heading. The share price rose immediately to $111.5, sending the company's market value to almost $2 trillion, before falling by the end of the day, with shares hitting $97. items.headline: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months
items.blurb: US House committee releases chip export data amid scrutiny of former Nvidia CEO's alleged links to a Chinese spy.
items.text: The administration of United States President Donald Trump approved exports of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee has said. The Department of Commerce’s approvals covered exports of 879,000 chips, including 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD, the committee said on Thursday. Companies had sought permission to ship 3.4 million of them to China during the period, committee documents show. The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the Trump administration faces heightened scrutiny following revelations about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy , which fuelled renewed calls for a tougher stance against Chinese technology threats. All four of the Chinese companies highlighted in the committee report are on the Pentagon’s list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies. items.headline: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
items.blurb: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
items.text: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia. The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa , on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions. The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer. The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago , when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park , owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. items.headline: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, top UN court rules
items.blurb: The unprecedented International Court of Justice verdict concerns a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands.
items.text: Myanmar has been found guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority by the International Court of Justice (ICJ). The verdict marks the first time a state has ever been found to have committed genocide by an international court. Yuji Iwasawa, president of the UN's top court, said Myanmar had the "intention to destroy" a substantial part of the Rohingya population and engaged in "extensive destruction of evidence" to hide its crimes. A military crackdown in 2017 killed thousands of Rohingya and forced more than 700,000 to flee Buddhist-majority Myanmar, formerly known as Burma. Myanmar denied the claims against it, saying its forces had responded to attacks by armed groups. The court found on Thursday that "genocidal intent is the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from the evidence" it had seen. The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world. The ICJ also found in favour by majority that Myanmar had violated several other parts of the 1948 Genocide Convention. The case brought by The Gambia

items.headline: Haiti police say at least 34 suspected gang members killed in raid
items.blurb: Police say the raid targeted the Martissant area, located on a key route out of Port-au-Prince held by gangs since 2021.
items.text: At least 34 suspected gang members were killed in a police operation in Martissant, a neighbourhood in Haiti’s capital that has been under gang control for more than five years, Haitian police said. Haiti’s National Police, which posted footage of armoured vehicles moving through the neighbourhood, said their officers carried out the raid on Thursday with an anti-gang task force that includes personnel from Vectus Global, the private security firm founded by Blackwater founder Erik Prince. Police reported no other casualties and said none of the roughly 2,500 Salvadoran troops in Haiti took part. The Martissant neighbourhood is located along a key road that connects Port-au-Prince to Haiti’s western and southern cities, and was used by thousands of people daily before rival gangs began fighting to control the area in 2021. The subsequent violence forced at least 19,000 people to flee their homes, according to a July 2022 UN report. items.headline: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
items.blurb: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.
items.text: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund ( UNFPA ) published on Thursday. Younger women and girls aged 15 to 19 had even less power to say no, compared with older women aged 45 to 49, according to analysis in the report of eight countries with comparable data (Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mali, Nigeria, Tajikistan and Zambia). items.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi release 'peace declaration' after historic meeting
items.blurb: While the presidents have previously met for one-on-one meetings, this is their first trilateral discussion.
items.text: US President Donald Trump and his Russian and Chinese counterparts Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping have issued a "joint declaration of peace" following historic trilateral talks. The three leaders met for 90 minutes in China's south-eastern city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. While the presidents have previously had one-on-one meetings, these are their first trilateral talks. In the declaration, they said "nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought" and that the countries planned to increase the production and supply of petroleum. They also said they were "committed to reform the UN" to respond more effectively to global challenges. Thursday's statement also flagged the issue of immunity enjoyed by state officials and said "they agreed that the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction". Trump praised the trilateral meeting calling it "a great and highly consequential trip", in a social media post while flying back to Washington on Air Force One. items.headline: US appeals court lets Trump end TPS deportation protections for Venezuelans
items.blurb: The appeals court's ruling prevents a lower-court decision from taking effect, which would block Trump from lifting TPS.
items.text: A United States appeals court has allowed the administration of President Donald Trump to move forward for now with the removal of deportation protections for Venezuelans . The ruling on Wednesday cancels out a previous order by a lower-court judge that required the government to restore the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) of Venezuelans, which shields recipients against deportation. The effort to end the TPS protections has proceeded despite humanitarian concerns . Since taking office for a second term, Trump has sought to carry out what he calls the largest deportation effort in US history. Part of that agenda has been to roll back programmes like TPS. But in September 2025, US District Judge Edward Chen blocked the expiration of TPS protections for Venezuelans, arguing that deporting those individuals would put them in harm’s way. He also ruled that the Trump administration had overstepped its authority by seeking to shorten TPS extensions granted under the preceding president, Joe Biden. Such decisions, Chen added, needed to be taken with “careful study and analysis”. The Supreme Court paused Chen’s ruling in October 2025.

Lawyers representing Rohingya survivors say patterns of behaviour by Myanmar’s military, including killing people as they fled, show clear attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017. items.headline: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
items.blurb: European allies of Ukraine say they have a "united" negotiating position at a summit in Berlin.
items.text: European leaders have said they are ready for negotiations with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine, in a strong show of support for Kyiv. "Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic". They were speaking at Berlin's summit of Ukraine's allies known as the Coalition of the Willing. Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys who were in Berlin, said the US president wanted to make a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side". Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US-led peace talks. Trump had earlier held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen , south-eastern China, with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping and later dialled into the Berlin summit from Air Force One. In a lengthy press conference following his talks with Trump and Xi, Putin addressed the question of multilateral peace talks, saying the Americans were "insistently" asking Russia to allow the Europeans to take part.

items.headline: Resignation not admission of wrongdoing, I am innocent: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha secretariat
items.blurb: Resignation not admission of wrongdoing, I am innocent: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha secretariat
items.text: New Delhi, Justice Yashwant Varma has asserted that he is innocent of the allegations relating to the discovery of burnt currency notes at his official residence and that his resignation as a high court judge should not be construed as an acknowledgement or admission of any wrongdoing or of the findings against him. In a letter to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh on September 10 – which was circulated among MPs on Thursday – Varma also contended that proceedings for his removal had become infructuous following his resignation on April 9, and any attempt to remove him from office would be without constitutional foundation. Citing Article 217 of the Constitution and a 1978 Constitution Bench judgment of the Supreme Court in 'Union of India vs Gopal Chandra Mishra', he argued that a high court judge's resignation takes effect by its own force and does not require acceptance by the President or any other authority. items.headline: Several Bengal districts under alert as cyclone Akvan likely to bring heavy rainfall
items.blurb: Squally winds of 40–50 km/h, gusting to 60 km/h, along and off the West Bengal coast will prevail till Friday noon and ease afterward, with very rough sea conditions, says IMD
items.text: Commuters make way through rain-slicked roads in Kolkata on November 19, 2026. | Photo Credit: ANI Several districts in the southern part of West Bengal, including Kolkata, will receive heavy rainfall until November 21 due to the cyclonic storm Akvan. The storm, which lay over the east-central Bay of Bengal on Thursday morning (November 19, 2026), is expected to make landfall around noon on Friday (November 20, 2026), along the coast between Narsipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and Puri (Odisha), close to Gopalpur. Office-goers and daily commuters use umbrellas as heavy rainfall lashes the area outside Bidhannagar Railway Station in Kolkata on November 19, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a warning of heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and gusty winds in Kolkata, North 24 Parganas, Howrah, Hooghly, and Purulia districts, while South 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, Jhargram, and Bankura are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall. Since Wednesday night (November 18, 2026), Kolkata and several other south Bengal districts have experienced overnight and morning rainfall under the influence of the weather system.

items.blurb: Rahul Gandhi said said it was impossible for India to hold talks with Pakistan while innocent people continued to be killed.
items.text: India and Pakistan can work together but only if Islamabad stops supporting and encouraging terrorism in India, LoP in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has said. Interacting with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday, the Congress leader said it was impossible for India to hold talks with the neighbouring country while innocent people continued to be killed. Gandhi was responding to a question from a participant who identified himself as a Pakistani national. He asked Gandhi whether the two neighbouring countries could “move beyond the blame game and work together for mutual benefit” without allowing external factors to exploit their differences. “There is room, but there is a big problem, which is the support and encouragement of terrorism by Pakistan in our country,” Rahul Gandhi said. “And it is impossible for us to accept our innocent people being murdered and having a conversation with Pakistan. items.text: A First Information Report (FIR) has been lodged against two former Ministers in the West Bengal government, Indranil Sen and Bratya Basu, along with several senior government officials, over multiple charges, including sexual assault. The FIR was lodged at Baguiati Police Station under the Bidhannagar Commissionerate by social activist Rajib Sarkar on behalf of multiple women who have either been artists or employed by the West Bengal Information and Cultural Affairs Department. The two Ministers have been accused of rape, wrongful confinement, extortion, criminal breach of trust, cheating, repeated sexual assault, corruption and criminal conspiracy. “Several women approached me and levelled serious allegations against the two ministers. They have been threatened, harassed, and tortured when they asked for what they deserved. They should now get justice,” said Mr. Sarkar, speaking to the media. A zero FIR has been registered against 40 accused individuals, including the two former Ministers, he said. items.blurb: Maharashtra puts non-essential construction on hold in 304 drought-hit talukas, prioritises relief
items.text: The Maharashtra government has directed district authorities to temporarily suspend non-essential new construction works in 304 drought -hit talukas and divert available funds for drinking water supply and other drought-mitigation measures. A Government Resolution issued by the Planning Department on Wednesday said funds under the District Annual Plan (General) must be prioritised to finish incomplete water supply projects, strengthen existing water sources and ensure water and fodder availability for livestock. The state has identified 304 talukas as drought-affected, and the government said immediate measures were necessary to meet the drinking water requirements of citizens, livestock and other essential needs. District collectors have been directed to review non-essential new projects, including parks, beautification works, new office and administrative buildings, cement roads, drains and other works involving substantial water consumption, and take steps to temporarily defer them in accordance with prescribed procedures. Funds available for such deferred projects will be reviewed and reallocated to priority drought-relief works in the affected talukas, the GR said, adding that the exercise of reallocation must be completed by December 31. items.headline: Retail Investors Dive Into Both Sides of the Anthropic Trade
items.blurb: Retail traders rushed to buy — and sell — Anthropic PBC shares in one of the busiest market debuts on record Thursday.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- Retail traders rushed to buy — and sell — Anthropic PBC shares in one of the busiest market debuts on record Thursday. Non-professional investors’ net buying of Anthropic shares was on track to reach between $80 million and $90 million by the end of the day, according to Vanda Research. That would make it the third-biggest listing day on record, trailing SpaceX’s $118 million earlier this year and Coinbase Global Inc.’s $92 million in 2021, Vanda’s Viraj Patel wrote in a note. Total turnover by retail traders — including buying and selling — was poised to reach $1.4 billion, some three times as much as SpaceX’s turnover and a “record for a listing day by a wide margin.” “Retail are trading the stock hard,” Patel said. He noted traders were “taking both sides rather than a one-way bid.” Those investors sold single stocks to pay for Anthropic purchases, Patel added. The next two competitions are expected to fetch as much as $4 billion, with at least $2 billion for the 2030 event and $1 billion to $1.5 billion for 2034, one of the people said. The tender process is for the 2030 tournament with an option to bid for 2034 as well, according to FIFA. Skydance and ESPN had been expected to compete with other potential bidders including Netflix Inc., Fox Corp., Comcast Corp.’s NBC and Amazon.com Inc. items.headline: US Sour Crude’s War Premium Vanishes as Supply Surges
items.blurb: The price of US sour oil has plunged, as a surge of oil from Venezuela, Canada and the Middle East gives refiners ample barrels to choose from.
items.text: The price of US sour oil has plunged, as a surge of oil from Venezuela, Canada and the Middle East gives refiners ample barrels to choose from. US medium sour export grade Mars, which is pumped from deepwater wells in the Gulf of Mexico and is similar to Middle Eastern crude, traded at a record premium to benchmark West Texas Intermediate futures in the early days of the Iran war as buyers hunted for alternate supplies to those disrupted by the closed Strait of Hormuz. Now, as oil markets begin to settle after a volatile year, Mars has fallen to a steep discount, making it cheaper for US refiners built to process heavier crude. Mars has dropped from a $10 premium to a $4 discount to WTI futures in less than a month. That’s the steepest discount since late September. At the peak of Middle Eastern oil supply disruptions in March and April, it notched a record $17.50 premium even as futures traded for over $100 a barrel. items.headline: InPrime Finserv raises Rs 101 Cr in Series B round led by FMO
items.blurb: Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. Existing investors Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India) and Pravega Ventures also participated in the round.
items.text: Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. Existing investors Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India) and Pravega Ventures also participated in the round. The fresh capital will be used to expand the company's lending operations, strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities across underwriting and customer service, and diversify into micro-mortgage products, InPrime Finserv said in a press release. The company also plans to deepen investments in agentic AI and AI co-pilots to improve credit assessment and customer engagement. Founded by Sneh Thakur, Manish Raj and Rajat Singh in 2021, InPrime began operations in 2023. The company is an AI-first non-banking financial company (NBFC) focused on India's emerging middle class, particularly customers operating in the informal economy, including kirana store owners, dairy farmers, beauty parlour owners, small retailers and micro-entrepreneurs. NASA’s internal communication network went down. The FAA had to ground all flights for hours (only the third time in history since 9/11), and Microsoft was hit with an outage that took down Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for nearly two days. items.text: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.” “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.” In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating

All told, the offering will raise over $81 billion, directed to a combination of employees and the company’s own coffers. The IPO funding, together with existing fundraising and new private offerings timed to coincide with the company’s public market debut, will leave Anthropic with an expected $220 billion in cash reserves. As one analyst told TechCrunch , “Anthropic’s going to have more cash on hand than any company has ever had.” The share price continues to fluctuate, but the opening price would put the company’s market cap over $2 trillion, making it more valuable than Meta, Tesla, or Walmart. items.text: August AI has raised $12 Mn from Accel, Peak XV Partners, and Claypond Capital to expand its AI-powered healthcare assistant in the US. The startup is expanding beyond answering health questions to handling administrative tasks for patients, including calling doctors’ offices and following up on insurance claims. Its new AI agent is available through a US waitlist, while its existing August Care membership offers telehealth consultations, discounted lab tests, and prescription services. AI healthtech startup August AI has raised $12 Mn from Accel, Peak XV Partners, and Claypond Capital to expand its healthcare assistant’s ability to book appointments, find medicines, and follow up on insurance claims for users in the US. Founder and CEO Anuruddh Mishra announced the fundraise on social media alongside the rollout of the new capabilities. The startup claims to have helped 10 Mn people understand their health through its AI companion. The development comes after Inc42 exclusively reported in August that the startup was in talks to raise around $4 Mn from Peak XV Partners, with the terms still under discussion.
